content: Cip1-interacting zinc finger protein, encoded by the CIZ1 gene in humans, is a zinc finger DNA-binding transcription factor. This protein interacts with CIP1, also known as p21 or CDKN1A, which is a key regulator of the cell cycle. CIZ1 is part of a complex that includes cyclin E, and it may play a role in modulating the cellular localization of CIP1. In the context of clinical significance, an altered circulating form of the CIZ1 protein is produced by lung cancer cells, even at very early stages of the disease. This specific variant of the protein can potentially serve as a biomarker for the early detection of lung cancer when identified in the bloodstream. Additionally, CIZ1 has been demonstrated to interact directly with p21, further emphasizing its involvement in cell cycle regulation and its potential implications in cancer biology.
